Rashi on Shabbat 104a:10:1.english: I shall desire him - [This is said] as a rhetorical question, and so [too] all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:10:2.hebrew: ע"כ מדת הרשעים - כן הוא נדרש אצל רשעים:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:10:2.english: To this point [is] the attribute of the wicked - Thus it is expounded regarding the wicked.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:1.english: If you are ashamed - [To refrain] from sinning.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:2.hebrew: גר דק גור בדוק - נפשך תהא צרורה תחת כסאי, ודוק — שמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:2.english: Gimmel reish, dalet kuf: reside in dok [gur bedok] - Your soul shall be bound under My throne, and dok [means] heaven.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:3.hebrew: לים כל - גיהנם קרוי ים כל, לפי שהרוב הולכים שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:3.english: To the sea, all - Gehenna is called yam kol [sea of all], because the majority go there.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:4.hebrew: אמר שר של גיהנם - לים שלי, תן את כל העולם ואפילו ישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:11:4.english: The minister of Gehenna said - To my sea, give the entire world, and even Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:1.hebrew: אמר ליה אח"ס בט"ע גי"ף - אלפא ביתא היא אצל א"ת ב"ש, וכולן סדורות בספר יצירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:1.english: He said to him: Alef ḥet samekh, bet tet ayin, gimmel yod peh - It is an alphabet [system] alongside Atbash, and all of them are arranged in Sefer Yetzirah.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:2.english: I will have mercy on them because they spurned gif - Adultery.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:3.english: Dalet kaf tzadi - [This is] a notarikon [acronym for]: pure, honest, righteous.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:4.hebrew: אין לך - גיהנם, חלק בהן בישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:4.english: You have no - [You,] Gehenna, [have no] portion in them, [i.e.,] in Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:5.hebrew: ומרזן שת - ואומר שר של גיהנם: זונני מזרעו של שת — כל העובדי כוכבים וישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:12:5.english: Vav mem reish zayin nun, shin tav - And the minister of Gehenna says: "Sustain me from the seed of Seth" — [meaning] all idolaters and Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:1.english: Al bam - The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: You shall have no portion in them.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:2.hebrew: ג"ן ד"ס - אמר הקב"ה: אוליכם לגן הדס, לגן עדן:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:2.english: Gimmel nun, dalet samekh - The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I will lead them to the garden of myrtle [gan hadas], [that is,] to the Garden of Eden.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:3.english: Heh ayin, vav peh - Behold, I am faint with hunger.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:4.hebrew: ז"ץ ח"ק - הללו זרעו של יצחק הם, ולא אתנם לך:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:4.english: Zayin tzadi, chet kuf - These are the descendants of Isaac, and I will not give them to you.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:5.hebrew: ט"ר י"ש כ"ת - שמור לי והמתן, יש לי כתות אחרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:13:5.english: Tet reish, yod shin, kaf tav - Wait for me and tarry; I have other groups.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:1:1.hebrew: עלויי קא מעלי ליה - שהיתה מם סתומה בלוחות, אבל מם פתוחה לא היתה בלוחות, כדמפרש: "מנצפך צופים אמרום". וכיון דאמר רב חסדא: "מם וסמך שבלוחות בנס היו עומדים", לא אפשר לאוקומיה אלא בסתומה, דהואיל והכתב היה נראה משני עבריהם, היה לה ליפול אם לא שבנס היה עומד; אבל פתוחה אין בה נס. ע"כ מנצפך דרבי ירמיה דאמר "צופין אמרום", בפתוחים קאמר. יש שמקשין סוגיא זו על סוגיא דאמר במגילה, דרמינן הא דר' ירמיה אהא דרב חסדא, אלמא תרוייהו בסתומין! ואין זו קושיא, שכן דרך הש"ס מהפך הסברא כאן כדי שיקשה, ובמקום אחר מהפכו לפי הקושיא; ואי הוה בעי התם לתרוצי כי איתמר דרב חסדא בסתומין ודר' ירמיה בפתוחין — הוה מתרץ ליה, אלא תירוצא מעליא שני ליה התם, וה"נ:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:1:1.english: He elevates its [status] - For the closed mem was in the Tablets, whereas the open mem was not in the Tablets, as [the Gemara] explains: "The prophets instituted [the forms of] mem, nun, tzadi, peh, [and] kaf." And since Rav Ḥisda said: "The mem and samekh that were in the Tablets stood miraculously," it is impossible to establish [that statement] except with respect to the closed [mem], for since the writing was visible from both sides of [the Tablets], [the center piece] would have fallen had it not been standing miraculously; whereas an open [mem] involves no miracle. Therefore, [the] mem, nun, tzadi, peh, kaf of Rabbi Yirmeya, who said "the prophets instituted them," refers to the open ones. There are those who raise a contradiction between this sugya and the sugya stated in [Tractate] Megillah, where we contrast this [statement] of Rabbi Yirmeya with that [statement] of Rav Ḥisda — thus implying that both refer to the closed [forms]! However, this is not a difficulty, for such is the way of the Talmud: it reverses the reasoning here in order to raise a difficulty, and in another place reverses it according to the question; and had [the Gemara] wished there to answer that Rav Ḥisda's [statement] was said regarding the closed [forms] and Rabbi Yirmeya's regarding the open [forms], it could have answered it [that way], but instead it gave a better answer there, and so too [here].

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:2:1.hebrew: מיהוה הוה - תרוייהו, ולא ידעי הי באמצע תיבה כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:2:1.english: They existed - both of them [i.e., both the open and closed forms], and they did not know which [was used] in the middle of a word, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:3:1.hebrew: ונקרא מבחוץ - האותיות הפוכות והתיבה הפוכה. ולא אשמועינן אלא שהיה החקק נוקב את כל הלוח, ולפיכך היו מם וסמך בנס:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:3:1.english: And [it] was read from the outside - The letters are reversed and the word is reversed. And [it] only teaches us that the engraving pierced through the entire tablet, and therefore the mem and samekh [stood] miraculously.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:3:2.hebrew: נבוב בהר סרו - לא היו בלוחות, אלא תיבה בעלמא נקט:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:3:2.english: Nevuv, bahar, saru - [These words] were not on the tablets; rather, he merely cited a word [as an example].

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:4:2.hebrew: מ"ט פשיט כרעיה דגימ"ל לגבי דלי"ת - ולא לגבי בי"ת:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:4:2.english: Why is the leg of the gimmel extended toward the dalet - and not toward the beit?

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:4:3.hebrew: מ"ט פשיט כרעיה דדלי"ת לגבי גימ"ל - ולא לגבי ה"א, שמושכה קצת לצד גימ"ל:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:4:3.english: Why is the leg of the dalet extended toward the gimmel - and not toward the hei? For it extends slightly toward the side of the gimmel.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:4:4.english: That he should make available to him - the poor person [should make] himself [available], and not trouble the householder to run after him.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ו - כמו אני והו (סוכה דף מה.), שמות הם:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:1.english: Heh vav - Like "Ani VaHo" (Sukkah 45a); they are names [of God].

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:2.english: And bestows goodness upon you - That is [the letter] tet.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:5.english: In the World to Come - That is [the letter] lamed.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:6.hebrew: מאמר פתוח ומאמר סתום - יש דברים שנתן רשות לדורשן, ויש שאתה מצווה לסותמן, כגון מעשה מרכבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:6.english: An open statement and a closed statement - There are matters [regarding] which permission was given to expound them, and there are [matters] that you are commanded to conceal, such as the Account of the Chariot.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:7.hebrew: נאמן כפוף - אדם כשר צריך להיות כפוף ועניו, וסופו להיות פשוט וזקוף לעולם הבא:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:5:7.english: A bent faithful [person] - A worthy person must be bent and humble, and in the end he will be straight and upright in the World to Come.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:1.hebrew: סימנים - של סדר שמועות דתנא או אמורא בגירס', דלא תשכח אחת מהן, כגון אלו שבש"ס:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:1.english: Signs - [Mnemonic signs] for the order of traditions of a Tanna or an Amora in [one's] recitation, so that you do not forget one of them, such as those in the Talmud.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:2.english: An open mouth - At a time when [people] gather [and withhold Torah], scatter [and teach it].

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:3.hebrew: פה סתום - בשעת המפזרים כנס, אם יש גדול ממך:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:3.english: A closed mouth - At a time when [people] are scattering [Torah teachings], gather [your words] in, if there is someone greater than you.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:6:4.english: With bowing of [the] head - With trembling and extreme humility.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:7:1.hebrew: מ"ט מהדר אפיה דקו"ף מרי"ש - לישנא דמעליא הוא, שאחוריו של רי"ש לגבי הקו"ף, שאין הקב"ה רוצה להסתכל בפני רשע:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:7:1.english: Why does the kuf turn its face away from the reish - It is a euphemism, for the back of the reish is [turned] toward the kuf, because the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish to look at the face of a wicked person.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:7:2.english: The crown of the kuf - Like a kind of zayin that they make at the end of the roof of a kuf.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:7:3.english: The leg of the kuf is suspended - [That is,] it is not attached to its roof.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:1.english: Let him enter through that [opening] - Let him go around under the legs of the kuf and enter through the opening on the right.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:2.english: They assist him - And they prepare an opening for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:3.hebrew: הוא יליץ - מעצמו יליץ, לא יסייעוהו ולא ימנעוהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:3.english: He scorns - Of his own accord he scorns; they neither assist him nor prevent him.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:4.english: And if [he is] among the humble - and he is drawn to a good trait:

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:8:5.english: He gives grace - They will assist him from Heaven.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:1.hebrew: מקרבן מיליה - אותיות קרובות, שלשתן קרובות כסדרן של אלפא ביתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:1.english: Its letters are adjacent - [Meaning] close letters; all three of them are close in the order of the alphabet.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:2.hebrew: אמת מרחקן מיליה - זו בתחילת אל"ף בית, וזו באמצע, וזו בסוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:2.english: [The letters of] emet [truth] are distant - One is at the beginning of the alphabet, one is in the middle, and one is at the end.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:3.english: On one foot - Each and every letter in it stands on one foot.

Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:4.hebrew: אמת מלבן לבוני - מושכבין תחתיה אותיותי' כמין לבינה, דאל"ף הרי יש לה ב' רגלים ומושבה טוב, ורגל השני רחב:
Rashi on Shabbat 104a:9:4.english: Emet [is set like] bricks - Its letters are laid down underneath like a brick, for [the letter] alef has two legs and its base is firm, and the second leg is wide.

Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:1:1.hebrew: גרועי קא מגרע ליה דאמר רבי חייא בר אבא מנצפך צופים אמרום - וא"ת: דהכא משמע דבפתוחה קאמר דצופים אמרום, ובפ"ק דמגילה (דף ב:) פריך עלה דר' חייא בר אבא מאלה המצות, שאין נביא רשאי לחדש דבר, ועוד "האמר רב חסדא: מם וסמך שבלוחות בנס היו עומדים" — משמע דר' חייא בסתומה איירי! ואור"י דהכי קאמר התם: "ועוד האמר רב חסדא" — ועוד, אי רבי חייא בר אבא בסתומה איירי, תקשה נמי דרב חסדא; אלא ודאי בפתוחה איירי. והא דנקט "מנצפך", ולא נקט להו כסדר אלפא ביתא — משום ד"מנצפך" משמע "מן צופים":
Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:1:1.english: "He diminishes its [status], as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: The prophets instituted mantzepach" - And if you ask: Here it implies that he is speaking of the open [form of the letters], which the prophets instituted; yet in the first chapter of Megillah (2b), [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba from [the verse] "These are the commandments," [teaching] that a prophet is not permitted to innovate anything, and furthermore [from], "Didn't Rav Ḥisda say: The mem and samekh in the tablets stood miraculously" — which implies that Rabbi Ḥiyya is speaking of the closed [form]! And Ri says that this is what [the Gemara] is saying there: "And furthermore, didn't Rav Ḥisda say..." — [meaning,] and furthermore, if Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba were speaking of the closed [form], Rav Ḥisda's [statement] would also be a difficulty! Rather, he is certainly speaking of the open [form]. And the reason he used [the order] mantzepach and did not list them in alphabetical order is because mantzepach implies min tzofim ["from the prophets"].

Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:3:1.hebrew: נבוב בובן בהר רהב - תימה, דאמאי נקט להו, כיון דלא הוה בלוחות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:3:1.english: Nevuv buvan, bahar rahav - It is astonishing: why did [Rav Ḥisda] cite them, since they were not on the Tablets?

Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:4:1.hebrew: א"ל לר' יהושע בן לוי אתו דרדקי כו' - בירושלמי ובבראשית רבה (ס' א) קאמר דר' אליעזר ור' יהושע הוו מאותן דרדקי, וחולק על הש"ס שלנו. והא דאמר בפרקי דר' אליעזר שלא למד ר' אליעזר תורה אלא עד שהיה גדול — היינו שלא עסק עד שנעשה גדול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:4:1.english: They said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Young students came, etc. - In the Jerusalem Talmud and in Bereishit Rabbah (1), it states that Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua were among those young students, and this disagrees with our Talmud. And as for that which it states in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, that Rabbi Eliezer did not study Torah until he was an adult — that means that he did not engage [in it] until he became an adult.

Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:8:1.hebrew: אית דגרסי בא ליטמא פותחין לו - כלומר, יש לו פתחים ליכנס; "בא ליטהר מסייעין אותו" — שפותחין לו פתח ליכנס, והיינו דומיא דלעיל דשביק ליה פתח ליכנס. ולהנהו דגרסי "בא ליטמא פותחין לו", צריך לומר ד"מסייעין אותו" הוי טפי מ"פותחין":
Tosafot on Shabbat 104a:8:1.english: There are those who have the reading: "One who comes to become impure, they open for him" - That is to say, he has openings to enter; "One who comes to become purified, they assist him" — [meaning] that they open an opening for him to enter, and this is similar to [what was said] above, that He leaves him an opening to enter. And according to those who have the reading "One who comes to become impure, they open for him," one must say that "they assist him" is more than "they open."
